# WO-2026-08-10-08 — An answer is not a shopping list
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

### What Warwick actually experienced, an hour ago, on his real shop

He photographed his list. It became `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64` with 35 lines and 8 question cards.
He answered them. **Every free-text answer he typed was ALSO ingested as a new shopping list**,
creating `SHOP-2026-08-10-M76`, `M77`, `M79`, `M82` — one per reply. His answers DID land
(6 of 8 questions are `answered`), so this is a double effect, not a lost answer.

**The route that was supposed to prevent exactly this already exists and is wired.**
`shopperIntake.js` takes a `claim` hook and its own comment says *"Route first: runIntake asks
this BEFORE treating a message as a shopping list, so an answer is never also eaten as a list."*
The claim is happening — the answers landed — and the list ingestion happens anyway.

**WP-B15-07 did not cause this; it revealed it.** Before that fix these replies collided with a
terminal row and vanished silently. Now each mints its own shop, which is how Warwick saw it.

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — A TYPED ANSWER IS NEVER ALSO A LIST. The headline.** A typed reply that is claimed as
an answer to an open question produces exactly ONE durable effect — the answer — and **creates
no shop row and no list item**. Establish by execution where the claim currently fails to
suppress ingestion; the defect is in the seam between `claim` and `onRecord`, not in the
router's classification. Prove with a test that drives the REAL `runIntake` → `onRecord` path
with a claimed message and asserts **zero** shops created.

**AC2 — A NEW SHOP NEVER INHERITS A DEAD SHOP'S LIST.** `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64` is bound to
`list_id 20`, the CANCELLED `SHOP-2026-08-10`'s list, so one item from the dead shop (id 210,
Warwick's own typed answer from the previous night) is now in his real week. **This is the
WP-B15-07 defect one layer down: shop identity was fixed and list identity was left with the
same date-keyed collision.** A shop created for a new inbound list must be bound to a list
containing only that list's items. Same rule as WP-B15-07: **do not revive, mutate or append to
anything belonging to a terminal shop.**

**AC3 — A NON-ITEM LINE CAN BE DROPPED THROUGH A SUPPORTED ROUTE.** There is currently none:
`correctLine` can only set `requested` or `needs_decision`, so a line that is not a real item
can only be answered (adding junk to the basket) or left open (blocking the shop forever).
Warwick is blocked on exactly this right now. Add the narrowest supported route to mark a line
as not-an-item so it stops blocking and never reaches a basket. **It must be auditable** — an
event, like every other status change — and it must NOT delete history.

**AC4 — A CARD MUST NOT CONTRADICT ITSELF.** `renderMessages.js:207` prints
*"No candidate products found."* on cards that, immediately above, list suggested products in a
Note. Warwick received several. Either there are candidates or there are not; the card must say
one true thing. Fix the rendering so the two halves cannot disagree.

**AC5 — A TRAILING PACK SIZE IS NOT AN ORDER QUANTITY.** `"ARIEL 4in1 PODS 33"` produced
`quantity 33` / `requested_qty 33` — thirty-three packs, roughly £300-400. The parser already
handles `"9 ROLLS"`, `"16 CAPSULES"` and `"4 x 500ml"` correctly and `"2pkts TWIX"` correctly;
it trips only on a **bare trailing number**, which in a product name is almost always a pack
size. Correct that, and **prove the leading-quantity cases still work** (`"4 x 4pts ARLA"` = 4,
`"2pkts TWIX"` = 2) — a fix that breaks those is worse than the bug.

**AC6 — REGRESSIONS FIRST, RED BEFORE GREEN.** For AC1, AC2 and AC5 write the test first and
prove it RED against current behaviour, quoting the executed failure. A regression written
after the fix cannot prove it reproduced anything.

**AC7 — MUTATION-PROVEN.** Mutate the AC1 suppression and the AC2 list-identity guard, prove a
NAMED test RED for each, restore byte-identical with sha256 quoted both sides. Mutate inside a
`git archive` export or restore in a `finally` — never leave the repo mutated.

**AC8 — NOTHING WRITTEN TO THE LIVE STORE.** `live_authority: none`. Warwick's shop is LIVE and
half-answered right now. Do not connect to the live database, do not repair his data, do not
touch `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64`. Larry has already cancelled the four junk shops through the
product route; that is done and is not yours.

## Inputs supplied

- The live evidence in this order's opening section — measured by Larry read-only during Warwick's actual shop. Re-verify anything you doubt from the code; you may NOT connect to the live database to check it.
- `services/asdair/intake/shopperIntake.js` — the `claim` hook, the `claimed` result array, and the ordering comments around `onRecord` / `state.write`. The intent is already documented there; the behaviour does not match it.
- `services/asdair/pipeline/runtime.js` §§108-186 `pollIntake` and its `persist`, and the `claim` closure construction above it.
- `services/asdair/pipeline/commands.js` — `correctLine` (line ~322) for AC3's shape, and `receiveList` (~166) for the list binding in AC2.
- `services/asdair/bot/renderMessages.js:207` — the AC4 contradiction.
- `Deliverables/2026-08-10-WO-B15-07-terminal-shop-collision.md` — the sibling fix one layer up. AC2 is the same defect at the list layer; read how WP-B15-07 solved it and stay consistent rather than inventing a second pattern.
- `Builds/BUILD-015-.../Assurance/veritas-wp-b15-07-3bf9e1e.md` — Veritas's HOLD, whose D-3 predicted a sibling path exactly like AC2.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- THE QUESTION-SURFACE REDESIGN. Warwick wants all questions on ONE card, free-text answers interpreted both for the shop and as durable household rules, and a visible answered/outstanding state. That is a separate order, being specified, and it is NOT yours. Do not start it, and do not half-build it inside AC4.
- Match quality. Warwick is rightly angry that "BATCHLORS MAC N CHEESE" was asked at all when the catalogue holds "Batchelors Pasta 'n' Sauce Mac 'n' Cheese". Report anything you notice; fix nothing.
- Repairing Warwick's live shop, its list, its items or its open questions.
- fetch-shopper-list.js's own offset defect (R1 from WP-B15-07) - still parked, still Warwick's call.
- Migrations. If AC3 genuinely needs a new status value, STOP and return that conclusion.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK FIRST, then HOLD** (SOP-022): outcome, plan, what this order failed to settle,
   what looks wrong. Do not implement until Larry accepts or amends. Warwick's ruling is settled;
   the mechanism is yours.
2. **AC1 IS THE PRIORITY.** If you can only land one thing, land that — every reply Warwick types
   currently makes junk. Do it first and say so in your return.
3. Baselines for all four suites, then the AC6 regressions RED.
4. Implement AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5. Keep each narrow; five small correct fixes, not a redesign.
5. Mutation proof per AC7, byte-identical restore.
6. Re-run all four suites; report counts.
7. **Git endpoint: COMMIT and PUSH `build-015/b15-08-answer-not-a-list`. No PR. Do NOT touch
   `main`. Do NOT merge.** Larry integrates, cuts the runtime over and commissions Veritas.
8. Return: what you changed, both mutation directions with sha256 pairs, suite counts, and
   anything you refused and why. If AC2 turns out to be larger than one order, say so early
   rather than delivering half of it silently.
